title: Blue Jays erupt for 5 runs in the eighth to beat Red Sox 6-4, extend Boston’s skid to 5
author: The Associated Press
bullets: Blue Jays scored 5 runs in the eighth inning to beat Red Sox 6-4, led by Kazuma Okamoto's RBI single.
Willson Contreras hit his 24th home run, tying Boston's longest losing streak of the season at five games.
Toronto improved its playoff position, winning three straight games and 11 of the last 16 in the AL wild-card race.

title: Allston-Brighton residents divided over future of Jackson Mann Community Center, survey shows
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: A city survey showed no consensus on the redevelopment of Jackson Mann Community Center in Allston.
Options included a mix of housing and a school, with different community preferences expressed.
Mayor Wu will decide on the site's future by year-end, with construction expected to start in 2030.

title: Tour the Patriots’ new 160,000-square-foot training facility
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: The New England Patriots unveiled the 160,000-square-foot New Balance Athletics Center, adjacent to Gillette Stadium.
The facility features a 15,000-square-foot weight room, a virtual reality room, and 92 locker spaces.
New Balance Athletics Center includes a players' lounge, dining facilities, and hydrotherapy room for player rehabilitation.

title: Man killed in stabbing inside South Station during rush hour, officials say
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A man was fatally stabbed inside South Station during rush hour on Wednesday evening, police reported.
The stabbing occurred following an altercation on an escalator; the suspect remains unidentified and at large.
Authorities are examining video evidence and interviewing witnesses to gather more details on the incident.

title: Body found at TD Garden, police say
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Boston police found a deceased person near TD Garden on Wednesday evening after responding to an unconscious person report.
The body was located around 5:15 p.m. at 100 Legends Way, the address for TD Garden.
The incident is under investigation, and preliminary reports suggest the person was in the adjacent parking garage.

title: Athol man charged with child pornography possession
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Kristopher Ambrozewicz, 35, of Athol, charged with possession of child pornography, federal prosecutors announced.
A search revealed child sexual abuse videos on Ambrozewicz's phone; electronics were seized for review.
Ambrozewicz served as youth soccer referee and works at a behavioral health center in Orange.

title: Police: Person held pregnant woman hostage with gun during dramatic chase on I-93 in Milton
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Dominic Hampton-Boyd, 31, was arrested after a police chase on I-93 in Milton involving a pregnant hostage.
The suspect crashed into eight vehicles before fleeing on foot; a firearm was seized from the SUV.
The hostage received medical care; her injury status is unknown. Hampton-Boyd faces charges in Quincy District Court.

title: Stoughton town manager contradicts police chief who accused him of tampering with Sandra Birchmore investigation
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Stoughton Town Manager Thomas Calter denies allegations of tampering with an investigation involving Sandra Birchmore.
Police Chief Donna McNamara filed a lawsuit accusing Calter of harassment and interfering with police investigations.
Calter and McNamara are on paid administrative leave amid a no-confidence vote by local unions against Calter.

title: Nearly 30 people arrested after investigation into drug trafficking in Western Mass.
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Twenty-eight individuals were arrested in a drug trafficking investigation in Chicopee, Holyoke, and Springfield, Massachusetts.
Officials seized over 12 firearms, more than 1 kilogram of cocaine, fentanyl pills, and heroin during the operation.
The investigation, named 'Operation Pinky Promise,' involved local and federal officials using various methods including surveillance and wiretaps.

title: Patriots stock watch 2.0: Who’s rising and falling ahead of preseason opener?
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Romeo Doubs excels in practice with a two-handed touchdown grab, boosting his stock before the Patriots' preseason opener.
Patriots rookie Caleb Lomu remains focused despite inconsistent training sessions, preparing for potential opportunities in the preseason.
Reserve cornerbacks struggle as Colts complete 11 straight passes, highlighting depth concerns in the Patriots secondary lineup.
